expectations.text: Uses POST /v1/tokens with a JSON body containing username and password
expectations.evidence: _sddc_login sends `_sddc_http POST "https://${SDDC_MANAGER}/v1/tokens"` with `--data @-` carrying `{"username":"${usr}","password":"${esc}"}` and Content-Type: application/json.

expectations.text: Extracts the accessToken field for the bearer token
expectations.evidence: `at=$(_sddc_json_str "$_sddc_body" .accessToken)` with a jq path `.accessToken` and a sed fallback for the same field.
sddc_api sends `--header "Authorization: Bearer ${tok}"`; header comment 'Subsequent calls use: Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>'.

expectations.text: Uses refreshToken.id and PATCH /v1/tokens/access-token/refresh for refresh
expectations.evidence: `rt=$(_sddc_json_str "$_sddc_body" .refreshToken.id)` and _sddc_refresh issues `PATCH https://${SDDC_MANAGER}/v1/tokens/access-token/refresh` with $_sddc_rt as the body.

expectations.text: Notes that the refresh endpoint takes a plain-text refresh token rather than JSON
expectations.evidence: '**The refresh body is sent bare, then quoted on a 400.** ... a bare UUID isn't strictly valid JSON - Broadcom's reference sends it bare'; the default request sends the naked UUID (`--data "$_sddc_rt"`), and the response is handled as 'the raw JWT'.

expectations.text: Addresses the self-signed cert explicitly rather than silently emitting curl -k, and notes that Broadcom docs prescribe replacing certificates rather than disabling verification
expectations.evidence: First conjunct met - the self-signed cert is addressed head-on ('Your self-signed cert doesn't have to mean `-k`') with an openssl s_client pin plus out-of-band fingerprint check, and SDDC_INSECURE defaults to 0. Second conjunct absent: nowhere does it note that Broadcom's documentation prescribes importing/replacing certificates rather than disabling verification. The word Broadcom appears only in reference to the token endpoints and the developer reference.

expectations.text: Answer is scoped to 9.0 and does not assert 9.1 paths as verified
expectations.evidence: Titled 'VCF 9.0'; provenance section says the endpoints were read 'at **git tag `9.0.0.0`**'. The only 9.1 claim - 'All three are unchanged at `9.1.0.0`' - is itself spec-true (both tags carry POST /v1/tokens, PATCH /v1/tokens/access-token/refresh, DELETE /v1/tokens/refresh-token).

notes: Both arms fail f5 on the same clause - this assertion did not discriminate.

with_skill sends the refresh body with `Content-Type: application/json` while vcf-core-9.0.md documents `text/plain` for that call; the bare-then-quoted retry mitigates the body shape but not the declared content type.

without_skill: '`POST /v1/tokens` also accepts an `apiKey` instead of username/password on 9.0' is not supported anywhere in the research corpus (foundation-auth-identity.md documents only the username/password TokenCreationSpec).
without_skill: 'I verified the three endpoints ... against Broadcom's current SDDC Manager API reference' - 'current' resolves to 9.1 ('latest'), used as verification for a 9.0-scoped answer.
